A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-inversion work despite retitling and a substantial solver revision. The text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary sections are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO reconstruction and editing experiments, a 60-image user study, and interpolation and rare-concept generation results, including supplementary examples.

after.justification: v2 reports RNRI experiments with latent diffusion and consistency models, comparative user studies, regularization ablations, and a convergence audit of 118,000 COCO image-caption pairs.

M1.justification: v1's fixed-point solver is replaced by a componentwise Newton–Raphson update using derivatives of an L1 residual plus Gaussian negative-log-likelihood regularization (v2 Sections 4–4.1, Equations 7–8). This changes the objective and inversion procedure substantially. The short prompt-aware preprocessing procedure is retained.

E1.justification: Both cover reconstruction, text-guided editing, seed interpolation, centroid finding, and rare-concept generation using COCO and ImageNet1k classes grouped by LAION2B prevalence. The LCM experiments change model configurations, while the larger COCO convergence audit examines additional samples and failures within existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's DDIM, Null-text, and EDICT comparisons, v2 evaluates AIDI and ExactDPM in LDM reconstruction and ReNoise in LCM comparisons. AIDI also enters editing, user-study, interpolation, and rare-concept comparisons. DDIM no longer appears in the LDM reconstruction plot, although it remains in other reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported backbone changes from Stable Diffusion 1.5 to 2.1, LCM configurations are added, and five FPI iterations become two RNRI iterations per diffusion step. New evaluations include guidance-scale 7.5 controls and the 118,000-pair convergence audit. User-study results now cover four LDM choices and a separate two-method LCM comparison. Reporting remains inconsistent: Section 5 specifies four LCM steps, while Figure 5 specifies two.

E4.justification: v2 expands the iteration analysis into a solver comparison, adds regularization ablation and lambda sensitivity (Figure 3 and Appendices C–D), and tests prompt-aware adjustment across solvers at high guidance scale (Table 1). Appendix G adds a large convergence audit and incorrect-caption failure cases. The original qualitative prompt-adjustment analysis and cake-to-hat editing failure are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and display error bars in Figure 3 without defining their statistical meaning. v2 follows this practice in its lambda plot and introduces no repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, confidence-interval definitions, or significance tests. The new convergence percentage is an additional outcome rather than a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Rare-concept results change from FPI's 87.3% tail accuracy, 95.0% total accuracy, and 6.4 FID to RNRI's 89.1%, 95.8%, and 6.3 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3). User preference changes from 61.7% in the original three-way comparison to 40.4% in the four-way LDM comparison, with a new 89.9% LCM preference against ReNoise. Changed methods, settings, and choice sets prevent interpreting these as controlled gains or losses. v2 adds LCM results, AIDI entries, and 95.4% convergence; the proposed interpolation/centroid numbers remain identical.

T1.justification: v1's conditional fixed-point contractivity argument is replaced by scalar residual and regularized-objective definitions, conditional Newton convergence discussion, and a Taylor-based componentwise update derivation in Appendix A. The inversion noise coefficient is also corrected from sqrt(alpha[t-1]) to sqrt(alpha[t]) in v2 Equations 3–4. The added derivation does not establish the asserted equivalence between a root of the regularized objective and its minimizer.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from fixed-point inversion to regularized Newton–Raphson inversion. v2 emphasizes convergence in one or two iterations and claims interactive editing at approximately 0.5 seconds with LCMs, whereas v1 emphasizes approximately five-second FPI editing. The prompt-adjustment claim expands from improving FPI to benefiting iterative inversion methods generally.

C2.justification: The original prompt-misalignment explanation remains, but v2 adds interpretations involving out-of-distribution roots, regularization strength, and amplification of inconsistency by guidance scale. Its new limitations section and Appendix G connect convergence failures to incorrect captions and suggest mismatch detection as a future application. v1's dismissal of Newton–Raphson as impractical is replaced by a proposed workaround for its Jacobian cost.

D1.justification: v2 adds PyTorch automatic differentiation and regularization information, with lambda 0.1 favored by the sensitivity analysis; the numerical stabilizer's value remains unspecified. The 512-by-512 input size and A100 hardware are retained. v1's square-cropping and scheduler-stride specifications, detailed time-capped baseline settings, and promise of public code upon acceptance disappear, without replacement code-access instructions.

R1.justification: Fixed-point inversion, presented as the main novelty in v1, becomes an approach attributed to prior AIDI work in v2. The revised positioning distinguishes RNRI from AIDI, ExactDPM, and ReNoise, adds consistency/distillation literature, and expands discussion of stochastic DDPM inversion, including LEDITS++, while explicitly excluding that family from the paper's scope.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries become a separate section, rare-concept background moves into the experimental discussion, and supplementary Sections 6–10 become Appendices A–G. Forward/backward terminology and author information are also revised.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. v2 redesigns the opening figure, expands performance plots and qualitative grids into LDM/LCM comparisons, and adds prior and failure displays. The original user-study table becomes prose, while a new ablation occupies Table 1. Retained material is also rearranged: v1 Figures 13–15 reappear as Figures S5, S6, and S1.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical scrutiny through closer baselines, regularization and guidance ablations, and quantified failure analysis. However, its new central formulation asserts a root/minimizer equivalence that its Gaussian log-density objective and Appendix A do not justify. Conflicting LCM step counts also leave the headline speed evidence ambiguous. These issues affect the mathematical foundation and performance interpretation, so the substantial empirical additions do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
